openai.feedback:
- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/lib/plan_design_check.py:166–167
- Finding: Design extensions and contradiction lines suppress mismatch findings just like recorded decisions. For example, a section specifying `"Thread bord"` passes against a screen showing `"Thread board"` if an extension line mentions `"Thread bord"`, even though no decision resolves that mismatch. This lets an autonomous plan pass the gate and reach Build with an unresolved difference.
- Suggestion: Suppress detected mismatches only when a covering `Design decision:` resolves them. Handle genuine additions and undecidable contradictions separately rather than treating every note as a resolution.

- Category: bug
- Severity: medium
- File: shared/scripts/lib/plan_design_check.py:222–223
- Finding: A missing referenced screen is silently ignored. If the Design Reference contains a stale or misspelled filename, `_screens_for` returns no screens and the checker passes without comparing the section’s text, breakpoints, or colors.
- Suggestion: Report missing referenced screens as problems in autonomous runs and as notes in interactive runs, so the check cannot silently succeed without its comparison source.

Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The gate integration implements the intended workflow, but these two bypasses allow autonomous plans to pass without the required design verification.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

glm.feedback:
Review complete. Findings:

- Category: test | Severity: medium
  File: plugins/shipwright-build/tests/test_design_decision_resolved.py:11–26
  Finding: These are substring-grep tests over markdown prompt files. They verify only that certain sentences exist in SKILL.md/spec-reviewer/requirement-writeback, not that any agent or checker behaves accordingly. A regression that reverts the behavioral wiring while leaving the prose intact (or vice versa) passes. Notably `test_writeback_reference_documents_the_rule` would pass if the reference contradicted the SKILL, since only two phrases are checked.
  Suggestion: This is partially unavoidable for prompt plugins, but at least assert the *pairing* (e.g. that the SKILL's "resolved" paragraph and the writeback's "resolved" paragraph name the same winner set: `screen` and `brief`), and assert that `Design extension` is still NOT an exemption in the reviewer, which the plan-side tests cover but these don't.

- Category: bug | Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-plan/scripts/checks/check-design-contradictions.py:46–48
  Finding: The dedup check requires both `**Section:** {heading}\n` and `**Decision:** {d[:500]}` to appear verbatim in the decision log. If `write_decision_log.py` performs any markdown escaping/normalization of `->`, quotes, or trailing whitespace, the substring test silently fails and the same decision is logged repeatedly on re-run. The test `test_record_decisions_logs_once` covers one benign decision string only.
  Suggestion: Confirm `write_decision_log.py` emits the decision verbatim for adversarial strings (arrows, backticks, quotes), or make the dedup key structural (parse headings + decisions) rather than raw substring.

- Category: bug | Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-plan/scripts/checks/check-design-contradictions.py:33
  Finding: `_decisions` globs `sections/*.md` but the dedup heading uses `planning.name/{sec.stem}`. If two planning dirs share a section filename (multi-split plans with identically-named sections under different splits), a decision logged for split A suppresses logging the identical decision for split B, since `planning.name` distinguishes them only if the CLI is invoked per-split — which it is, via `--planning-dir`, so this is safe in practice. No action needed; flagging only to confirm `planning.name` is the split name at invocation time.
  Suggestion: None — verify `planning_dir.name` equals the split name used in the gate's `decisions_recorded` check to avoid divergent dedup keys.

- Category: edge-case | Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/lib/plan_design_check.py:169–177 (`breakpoint_mismatch` block)
  Finding: `if m.media and not m.external_css` means a single `<link rel="stylesheet">` anywhere in any referenced screen disables the breakpoint check for all screens combined. A screen that inlines its breakpoints plus links a kit stylesheet hides real 768px-vs-900px mismatches. Tests document this as intentional (conservative), but the combined-model design makes one screen's link suppress findings for *other* screens' breakpoints too.
  Suggestion: If suppression per-screen matters, track `external_css` per screen and only skip widths while still checking widths declared against screens that inline their own `@media`. Otherwise document the whole-model suppression.

- Category: edge-case | Severity: low
  File: shared/scripts/lib/plan_design_check.py:126–131 (`_literals`)
  Finding: `visible_vs_attribute` fires only when the line contains one of `button|label|text|reads?|says?|shows?|caption` and lacks an "excuse" word. A section line like `- the control displays "Previous thread"` (or non-English) evades the check. Conservative-by-design is fine for a near-miss checker, but worth noting the heuristic is narrower than the docs ("compares quoted UI text") imply.
  Suggestion: None required; consider widening the trigger word list or noting the limitation in the docstring.

- Category: test | Severity: low
  File: plugins/shipwright-plan/tests/test_design_check.py:141–156 (`test_cli_in_process_and_failed_log_write_is_a_problem`)
  Finding: The test loads the CLI via importlib and monkeypatches `subprocess.run` with a stub whose `run` ignores arguments entirely — it doesn't verify the subprocess was called with the right script path or decision payload, only that a nonzero rc becomes a problem. A wrong `--decision` payload would still pass.
  Suggestion: Capture args in the stub and assert `write_decision_log.py` is invoked with the section heading and decision text.

Positive notes: mode detection (`is_autonomous_design_run`) handles missing/corrupt/non-dict config safely; interactive runs provably never fail (problems only when autonomous, verified by `test_interactive_run_is_unchanged` and `test_design_problems_modes`); the `check-plan-gates.py` integration correctly takes only `[0]` so notes never block; the CLI paths (`parents[4]/shared`) resolve correctly; the boundary-gate-allowed new files (`CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/`, `.shipwright/`) don't trip the boundary check. The lib tests exercise real finding logic including false-stop regressions, not just prose.

Overall: sound implementation of the spec; the findings are refinements to test rigor and dedup robustness rather than functional defects. Ship-as-is is defensible, but the decision-log dedup fragility is worth a quick confirmation against `write_decision_log.py`'s actual output format.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve
